parameters.content:
## Version 5 Voice Dental Assistant (Vapi + Twilio)
This workflow is a TOOL BACKEND, not the conversation itself. The live phone call is handled entirely by a Vapi Assistant (see ../vapi/assistant-config.json + ../VAPI-VOICE-SETUP.md) — Vapi does STT/LLM/TTS and calls this workflow's webhook only for side effects that need real data (booking, lookup, calendar, logging).

### Flow
Webhook (POST, one URL for everything Vapi sends) → Parse Vapi Message → Load Clinic Config → Message Type? (tool-calls / end-of-call-report / other)
  • tool-calls → Expand Tool Calls → Route Tool (Switch on function name) → 7 tool branches, each: FAST path computes the result Vapi needs to keep talking → Collect Tool Results → Respond (one JSON response covering ALL tool calls in the message). A SLOW/async path (Sheets/Gmail/Twilio) branches off the same compute step and runs AFTER the response is already sent — it never blocks the live call.
  • end-of-call-report → log the full call to Conversations + update Patient_Records, then ack.
  • anything else → ack with {} (Vapi sends other message types too — must always get a fast 200).

### The 7 tools
lookup_patient, check_availability, book_appointment, cancel_or_reschedule_appointment, log_emergency, request_human_handoff, faq_lookup (optional — prefer Vapi's native Knowledge Base for lower latency; keep this as fallback).

### Credentials to set after import
Google Sheets → all Sheets nodes. Gmail → all Gmail nodes. Twilio → SMS nodes (gated off by default). Google Calendar → the 5 calendar nodes (calendar = moshiurrahman.rupu@gmail.com, set in Load Clinic Config). OpenAI + Pinecone → ONLY needed for the optional faq_lookup tool (embeddings, no chat model — the conversational model lives in Vapi and is billed/configured there separately).

### Webhook
Path: /webhook/vapi-dental-assistant (POST). Response Mode = 'Using Respond to Webhook Node' — required so the fast/slow split works. Point Vapi's Server URL at this webhook's production URL.

### Read this before going live
See VAPI-VOICE-SETUP.md §2 for the full latency checklist (model/voice/transcriber choice, Vapi native KB, tool filler messages, why nothing here calls an LLM in the hot path).

return [{ json: { sheet_id: d.sheet_id, timestamp: d.timestamp, session_id: d.session_id, user_message: (d.transcript || '').slice(0, 4000), bot_response: d.summary, intent: 'voice_call', confidence: '', urgency: '', patient_name: '', phone: d.phone, email: '', status: 'Logged', notes: (d.test_mode ? '[TEST] ' : '') + 'Call ended: ' + d.endedReason } }];

const results = $input.all().map(i => ({ toolCallId: i.json.toolCallId, result: typeof i.json.result === 'string' ? i.json.result : JSON.stringify(i.json.result) }));
return [{ json: { results } }];

parameters.content: Each tool branch below has a FAST chain (feeds → Collect Tool Results → Respond) that computes only what the spoken reply needs, and — where there's a side effect — a SLOW chain (Sheets/Gmail/Twilio) branching off the same point, which runs in parallel and does NOT feed the response. n8n sends the HTTP response as soon as the fast chain reaches Respond ToolCalls, regardless of whether the slow chain has finished — the live call is never blocked on logging or notifications.
